key_insight: The paper introduces quantum probabilistic local differential privacy, a relaxed privacy notion that allows rare privacy-violation events while preserving useful structural guarantees and enabling sample-complexity bounds for quantum hypothesis testing.
engineering_relevance: This gives quantum ML and quantum information pipelines a more flexible privacy model for designing private quantum channels, noise mechanisms, and statistical inference routines under realistic implementation constraints.
method: Defines quantum probabilistic local differential privacy via a low-probability spectral violation event.
Proves composition and unitary post-processing properties, and characterizes when depolarizing noise satisfies the criterion.
Connects the privacy notion to hockey-stick divergence and derives lower bounds on privatized contraction coefficients and hypothesis-testing sample complexity.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports analytical results and derived sample-complexity bounds rather than an empirical benchmark, simulation, or dataset evaluation.
watch_item: The relaxation is not convex and is not preserved by arbitrary quantum-channel post-processing, so practical deployment may require careful mechanism-specific verification.
paper_title: Quantum Probabilistic Local Differential Privacy: Structural Properties and Sample Complexity Bounds
